MemTrace (authors' own, no version; GitHub https://github.com/theseus-labs-rsi/MemTrace). Baselines: Native harness context management, Observation Masking (Lindenbauer et al. 2025), RepoGraph (Python only)

Immutable Memory Traces (execution evidence + provenance, repository state, entity bindings to files/symbols/tests, Memory Anchor); Memory Trace Graph (depend, verify, correct, supersede relations); Repository State Graph (files, symbols, tests; defines, calls, imports, covers); trace-entity projection; Trace Synopses; checkpoint of execution frontier. Tasks: DeepSWE (113), SWE-EVO (46), SWE-Milestone (98 milestones). Configurations: 2 harnesses x {Native, Obs. Masking, RepoGraph, MemTrace} + 4 ablations. Baseline: Native. Held constant: backbone model and harness within each setting, context window, no step limit. Acceptance: benchmark tests and official scoring. Repetitions: Not stated (apparently single run). Human intervention: none

MemTrace best primary metric in every benchmark-harness setting: DeepSWE +21.2 (Codex) / +17.7 (mini) points over best baseline; SWE-EVO +4.4 / +10.8; SWE-Milestone Score +17.8 / +13.8. Obs. Masking lower Fix Rate gap: higher Fix Rate than MemTrace under Codex (72.1 vs 70.6) but lower Resolved. Baselines sensitive to harness (Obs. Masking +17.4 under Codex, -28.3 under mini on SWE-EVO). No significance tests on performance

Distinguished MemTrace from baselines with large margins, but single runs and no uncertainty on performance; strong harness-dependence of baselines noted. Ablation shows RSG matters on DeepSWE but not on SWE-EVO. No limitations of the comparison discussed by the authors

No limitations or threats section. Future work: more backbone models and context-window sizes; persistent multi-task, multi-session settings in the same repository. Implementation scope: RSG symbol-level only for Python, file-level for other languages
